reason.en: the supplied inventory has uncompensated ionic charge. This adapter interprets non-H/O element totals as an analytical component problem and adjusts pH to impose electroneutrality; H/O basis entries are conservation coordinates, not prescribed free-ion concentrations. A reported pH or speciation therefore describes that proton-compensated analytical problem, not a prediction for a complete physical mixture of these ions. Supply the actual counterions or use complete acid, base or salt reagents; no sodium, chloride or other counterion is inferred

reason.en: this milk has been acidified to pH {ph}, and only half of its buffer is modelled. Its colloidal calcium phosphate is here and dissolves as the acid arrives; casein's own buffering is not here at all, and that is about a third of milk's buffer capacity. Above pH 5 what is missing costs little; below it the colloid is spent and this beaker has nothing left to resist with, where a real one still has casein — so the number is a lower bound again, and by more than it was. {assumption} (the recipe's full assumption is in `explain material whole_milk`)
